get_account.title: Get the account
get_account.description: Read the account behind the credentials -- its id, company name and default currency. The cheapest call that proves the token works.

list_sources.title: List sources
list_sources.description: Read every billing source connected to the account. Start here: the `id` of a source is the `source_id` every customer, plan, subscription and charge call needs, and the `provider` field tells you whether it is writable (`baremetrics`) or a read-only mirror of Stripe, Recurly or Braintree.

list_users.title: List Baremetrics users
list_users.description: Read the people who have access to this Baremetrics account, with their names and email addresses. Use it to resolve the `user_id` an annotation can be attributed to.

users.description: Each with id, name and email.

get_user.title: Get a Baremetrics user
get_user.description: Read one Baremetrics user by id -- name, email and role on the account.

user_id.description: The user's Baremetrics id, from list_users.

show_summary.title: Get the metrics summary
show_summary.description: Read every headline metric -- MRR, ARR, active customers, churn, ARPU, LTV -- over one date range, across the whole account. This is the call for "how is the business doing"; use show_metric when you want one metric's day-by-day series instead.

start_date.description: Start of the range as YYYY-MM-DD.

end_date.description: End of the range as YYYY-MM-DD.

output.description: The summary metrics for the range, under `metrics`.

show_metric.title: Get one metric over time
show_metric.description: Read a single metric's series over a date range -- mrr, active_customers, churn, arpu, ltv and the rest. `compare_to` adds the previous period alongside it, which is how you answer "is this up or down".

start_date.description: Start of the range as YYYY-MM-DD.

end_date.description: End of the range as YYYY-MM-DD.

compare_to.description: Also return the preceding period, for a like-for-like comparison.

metrics.description: One entry per interval, with value and date.

show_plan_breakout.title: Break a metric out by plan
show_plan_breakout.description: Read one metric split per plan over a date range -- which plans carry the MRR, where the churn is concentrated. Same metric names as show_metric.

metric.description: The metric to break out, e.g. "mrr" or "active_customers".

start_date.description: Start of the range as YYYY-MM-DD.

end_date.description: End of the range as YYYY-MM-DD.

list_customers.title: List customers
list_customers.description: Read a source's customers, newest first by default. `search` matches name and email, so it doubles as customer lookup when you only have an address.

search.description: Match against customer name and email.

sort.description: Field to sort by, e.g. "created" or "name".

output.description: A page of customers, with pagination under `meta`.

get_customer.title: Get a customer
get_customer.description: Read one customer by the `oid` you created them with -- profile, current plan and lifetime value.

oid.description: Your own identifier for the customer.

create_customer.title: Create a customer
create_customer.description: Create a customer record in a Baremetrics-provider source. `oid` is your own identifier and is how every later call addresses this customer, so use the id your own system already has. Create the customer before the subscription that references it.

source_id.description: The source's id. Must be a source whose provider is `baremetrics`.

oid.description: Your own unique identifier for this customer.

email.description: Customer email address, used for the profile lookup.

notes.description: Free-text notes shown on the customer.

created.description: When the customer signed up, as an ISO 8601 timestamp. Defaults to now.

update_customer.title: Update a customer
update_customer.description: Change a customer's name, email, notes or signup date. Only the fields you send are touched; the customer is addressed by the `oid` you created them with.

customer_oid.description: Your own identifier for the customer.

delete_customer.title: Delete a customer
delete_customer.description: Erase a customer and everything hanging off them. Their history leaves the metrics, so past MRR and churn numbers change -- there is no undo.

oid.description: Your own identifier for the customer.

output.description: Confirmation that the customer was deleted.

list_plans.title: List plans
list_plans.description: Read a source's plans -- name, amount, currency and billing interval. Needed before creating a subscription, which references a plan by `oid`.

output.description: A page of plans, with pagination under `meta`.

get_plan.title: Get a plan
get_plan.description: Read one plan by the `oid` you created it with -- price, interval and trial length.

oid.description: Your own identifier for the plan.

create_plan.title: Create a plan
create_plan.description: Create a plan in a Baremetrics-provider source. `amount` is in minor units of `currency` -- 1000 is $10.00 -- and `interval` with `interval_count` sets the billing period (month/1 is monthly, month/3 is quarterly).

source_id.description: The source's id. Must be a `baremetrics` provider source.

oid.description: Your own unique identifier for this plan.

name.description: Plan name as it should appear in Baremetrics.

currency.description: ISO 4217 currency code, lower case, e.g. "usd".

amount.description: Price in minor units of the currency (1000 = $10.00).

interval_count.description: How many intervals per billing cycle -- 1 with "month" is monthly.

trial_duration.description: Length of the free trial, in `trial_duration_unit`s.

update_plan.title: Rename a plan
update_plan.description: Change a plan's name. Baremetrics does not let the price or interval of an existing plan be edited -- create a new plan and move subscriptions to it instead, so historic revenue stays attributed correctly.

plan_oid.description: Your own identifier for the plan.

delete_plan.title: Delete a plan
delete_plan.description: Erase a plan. Subscriptions on it lose their plan, so revenue attributed to it disappears from the plan breakout -- there is no undo.

oid.description: Your own identifier for the plan.

output.description: Confirmation that the plan was deleted.

list_subscriptions.title: List subscriptions
list_subscriptions.description: Read a source's subscriptions -- who is on which plan, when they started and whether they have cancelled. Filter by `customer_oid` to get one customer's history.

output.description: A page of subscriptions, with pagination under `meta`.

get_subscription.title: Get a subscription
get_subscription.description: Read one subscription by the `oid` you created it with -- plan, customer, quantity and dates.

oid.description: Your own identifier for the subscription.

create_subscription.title: Create a subscription
create_subscription.description: Put a customer on a plan. The customer and the plan must already exist in the same source -- create them first -- and `started_at` is what the new and active subscription metrics count from.

source_id.description: The source's id. Must be a `baremetrics` provider source.

oid.description: Your own unique identifier for this subscription.

started_at.description: When the subscription began, as an ISO 8601 timestamp or a Unix time.

plan_oid.description: The plan's `oid`, which must already exist in this source.

customer_oid.description: The customer's `oid`, which must already exist in this source.

canceled_at.description: When it was cancelled, if you are backfilling a churned subscription.

quantity.description: How many seats or units of the plan. Defaults to 1.

discount.description: Discount in minor units, subtracted from the plan amount.

addons.description: Extra recurring charges alongside the plan, each {"oid": ..., "amount": <minor units>, "quantity": 1}.

update_subscription.title: Move a subscription to another plan
update_subscription.description: Change a subscription's plan, quantity, discount or add-ons. This is how upgrades and downgrades are recorded: `occurred_at` dates the change, so the upgrade and downgrade metrics land in the right period.

subscription_oid.description: Your own identifier for the subscription.

plan_oid.description: The plan to move the subscription onto.

occurred_at.description: When the change happened, ISO 8601. Defaults to now.

addons.description: Replacement add-on list; omit to leave the add-ons alone.

cancel_subscription.title: Cancel a subscription
cancel_subscription.description: Record a cancellation, keeping the subscription and its history. This is what the churn and cancellation metrics read, so prefer it to delete_subscription for anything that really happened.

subscription_oid.description: Your own identifier for the subscription.

canceled_at.description: When the cancellation took effect, ISO 8601 or Unix time.

delete_subscription.title: Delete a subscription
delete_subscription.description: Erase a subscription outright. Its revenue leaves the metrics as if it never existed, which is almost never what you want -- use cancel_subscription for a real churn event.

oid.description: Your own identifier for the subscription.

output.description: Confirmation that the subscription was deleted.

list_charges.title: List charges
list_charges.description: Read a source's charges over a date range, optionally narrowed to one customer or subscription. This is the transaction-level view behind the revenue metrics.

start.description: Only charges created at or after this date (YYYY-MM-DD).

end.description: Only charges created at or before this date (YYYY-MM-DD).

output.description: A page of charges, with pagination under `meta`.

get_charge.title: Get a charge
get_charge.description: Read one charge by the `oid` you created it with -- amount, currency, fee and status.

oid.description: Your own identifier for the charge.

create_charge.title: Create a charge
create_charge.description: Record a payment against a customer. `amount` and `fee` are in minor units; a `status` of "paid" counts toward revenue while "failed" feeds the failed-charge metric. Link it to a subscription to attribute it to a plan.

source_id.description: The source's id. Must be a `baremetrics` provider source.

oid.description: Your own unique identifier for this charge.

subscription_oid.description: The subscription this charge pays for, if any.

created.description: When the charge happened, ISO 8601. Defaults to now.

fee.description: Processor fee in minor units, subtracted from net revenue.

delete_charge.title: Delete a charge
delete_charge.description: Erase a charge. The revenue it carried leaves the metrics for that period -- there is no undo.

oid.description: Your own identifier for the charge.

output.description: Confirmation that the charge was deleted.

list_refunds.title: List refunds
list_refunds.description: Read a source's refunds over a date range, which is what the refund metric aggregates.

start.description: Only refunds at or after this date (YYYY-MM-DD).

end.description: Only refunds at or before this date (YYYY-MM-DD).

output.description: A page of refunds, with pagination under `meta`.

create_refund.title: Create a refund
create_refund.description: Record money given back on a charge. `amount` is in minor units and may be less than the charge for a partial refund; the charge must already exist in the same source.

source_id.description: The source's id. Must be a `baremetrics` provider source.

oid.description: Your own unique identifier for this refund.

charge_oid.description: The `oid` of the charge being refunded.

created.description: When the refund happened, ISO 8601. Defaults to now.

list_annotations.title: List annotations
list_annotations.description: Read the notes pinned to metric charts -- "raised prices", "launched on Product Hunt" -- with the metric and date each is attached to.

create_annotation.title: Create an annotation
create_annotation.description: Pin a note to a metric chart on a date, so a jump in the numbers carries its explanation. `global: true` shows it on every metric rather than the one named.

metric.description: The metric the note belongs to, e.g. "mrr".

date.description: The date it applies to, YYYY-MM-DD.

is_global.description: Show the note on every metric chart rather than just `metric`.

user_id.description: Baremetrics user to attribute the note to, from list_users.

delete_annotation.title: Delete an annotation
delete_annotation.description: Remove a note from the metric charts. Deleting it does not affect any metric value.

output.description: Confirmation that the annotation was deleted.

list_goals.title: List goals
list_goals.description: Read the account's metric goals -- the target each metric is meant to reach and by when -- so progress can be reported against them.

create_goal.title: Create a goal
create_goal.description: Set a target for a metric between two dates. Amounts are in minor units for money metrics (100000 is $1,000 MRR) and plain counts otherwise.

metric.description: The metric the goal tracks, e.g. "mrr".

start_amount.description: Where the goal starts from -- minor units for money metrics.

delete_goal.title: Delete a goal
delete_goal.description: Remove a metric goal. The metric itself is untouched; only the target goes away.

output.description: Confirmation that the goal was deleted.

list_segments.title: List segments
list_segments.description: Read the saved customer segments on the account, each with the query that defines it. Segments are how Baremetrics slices metrics by customer attribute.

list_segment_fields.title: List the fields a segment can filter on
list_segment_fields.description: Read every field a segment query may reference, with its type. Read this before writing a `query` for create_segment or search_segment.

create_segment.title: Create a segment
create_segment.description: Save a customer segment from a filter query. `query` is a list of filter objects over the fields list_segment_fields returns, e.g. [{"field": "plan_name", "operator": "eq", "value": "Pro"}].

query.description: Filter objects defining the segment, over the fields list_segment_fields names.

search_segment.title: Search customers by segment query
search_segment.description: Run a segment query without saving it and get the matching customers back, paginated. The read-only way to answer "who is on this plan and spending over X" before committing to a segment.

query.description: Filter objects to match on, same shape as create_segment's `query`.

sort.description: Field to sort the matches by.

output.description: The matching customers, with pagination under `meta`.

list_attribute_fields.title: List custom attribute fields
list_attribute_fields.description: Read the custom attribute fields defined on the account, with their ids. You need a field id before you can set its value on a customer.

set_attributes.title: Set custom attributes on customers
set_attributes.description: Write custom attribute values against customers, which is what makes them segmentable. Each entry is {"customer_oid": ..., "field_id": ..., "value": ...} using ids from list_attribute_fields.

attributes.description: Attribute assignments, each with customer_oid, field_id and value.

output.description: The result of the write, listing what was set.

list_cancellation_reasons.title: List cancellation reasons
list_cancellation_reasons.description: Read the churn reasons offered in the cancellation survey, with their ids and sort order -- the vocabulary behind the cancellation insight events.

create_cancellation_reason.title: Create a cancellation reason
create_cancellation_reason.description: Add a reason to the cancellation survey. `sort_key` decides where it sits in the list shown to a churning customer.

text.description: The reason as the customer sees it.

list_cancellation_events.title: List cancellation events
list_cancellation_events.description: Read the cancellation survey responses -- who churned and what reason they gave. This is the qualitative half of the churn story the metrics only count.

get_cancellation_event.title: Get a cancellation event
get_cancellation_event.description: Read one cancellation survey response by id, with its reason and free-text comment.

list_source_events.title: List source events
list_source_events.description: Read the raw event stream a source has produced -- the imports and changes Baremetrics recorded -- over a date range. Useful for auditing why a metric moved.

start.description: Only events at or after this date (YYYY-MM-DD).

end.description: Only events at or before this date (YYYY-MM-DD).

live_stream.description: Restrict to the live event stream rather than the full history.

output.description: A page of events, with pagination under `meta`.
